events.title: Meson first released
events.summary: Jussi Pakkanen released Meson 0.1 on March 2, 2013 — a fast, readable build system that generates Ninja files.
events.about: Meson uses a Python-like DSL in `meson.build` files — declare executables, libraries, and tests; Meson emits Ninja build files for speed. GTK, systemd, Mesa, and GStreamer adopted it as a modern alternative to Autotools and CMake. Example: `meson setup build && meson compile -C build` configures and compiles a C project cross-platform.

narrative.whyChosen: Meson offered a simpler, faster alternative to Autotools for large open-source C/C++ projects.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the build system of choice for GNOME, freedesktop, and major Linux infrastructure.
narrative.problemSolved: Autotools and CMake configs were verbose, slow to configure, and error-prone for contributors.

events.title: Node.js 0.10 released
events.summary: Node.js 0.10 shipped on March 11, 2013 with stable streams, domains for error handling, and the foundation for npm's explosive growth.
events.about: Node 0.10 was the first long-lived stable line for production: the streams2 API made piping data reliable; domains helped catch async errors. It powered the early npm ecosystem — Express, Socket.io, and Grunt all targeted 0.10.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 0.10 was the version that made Node.js credible for production servers.
narrative.whyImportant: Stable streams and a predictable release line accelerated npm package adoption.
narrative.problemSolved: Earlier 0.x releases broke APIs too often for enterprises to commit.

events.title: Autoprefixer released
events.summary: Andrey Sitnik released Autoprefixer on March 14, 2013 — a tool that adds vendor prefixes to CSS based on Can I Use browser data.
events.about: Autoprefixer reads plain CSS and inserts `-webkit-`, `-moz-`, and `-ms-` prefixes where needed — freeing developers from memorizing which browsers needed prefixed flexbox or gradients. It started as rework-vendors, became Autoprefixer within weeks, and later migrated to PostCSS — becoming one of the most-used CSS build tools in history.

narrative.whyChosen: Autoprefixer automated the most tedious part of writing cross-browser CSS.
narrative.whyImportant: It let authors write spec syntax and let tooling handle vendor-prefix churn.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers copied prefixed and unprefixed rules by hand for every new CSS feature.

events.title: Docker open-sourced
events.summary: dotCloud open-sourced Docker on March 20, 2013 — packaging apps as portable containers (Solomon Hykes had publicly demoed it at PyCon on March 15).
events.about: Docker images bundle an app and its dependencies; `docker run` starts containers identically on laptops, CI, and cloud VMs. It standardized 'build once, run anywhere' for microservices and dev environments. Kubernetes later orchestrated Docker containers at fleet scale.

narrative.whyChosen: Docker made Linux containers usable for everyday developers, not just kernel experts.
narrative.whyImportant: It launched the cloud-native era — images, registries, and compose files became universal DevOps vocabulary.
narrative.problemSolved: Deploying apps meant fragile snowflake servers; teams needed reproducible, isolated runtime environments.

events.title: HTC One (M7) released
events.summary: HTC released the HTC One (M7) — aluminum unibody and BoomSound — premium Android design reference.
events.about: The phone expanded Android's flagship landscape beyond Samsung and Google. Aluminum unibody and boomsound — premium android design reference.

narrative.whyChosen: The HTC One (M7) was a significant Android flagship.
narrative.whyImportant: Diverse Android flagships gave developers multiple hardware targets beyond Galaxy and Pixel.
narrative.problemSolved: Android needed credible flagship alternatives to Samsung and carrier-skinned phones.
